chunks: I said to Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him): The people of Mecca do not slaughter the cow (at the throat), but rather they slaughter in the upper chest (labbah). So what is your view regarding eating its flesh?
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They slaughtered it, and almost did not do it.
Do not eat except what is properly slaughtered (at the throat).'

key_terms.اللَّبَّةِ: Al-labbah — the jugular notch/upper chest hollow, the point of nahr
key_terms.فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ: Quranic quotation from 2:71 about the Israelites and the cow
key_terms.يَذْبَحُونَ: Dhabh — the Islamic method of slaughter by cutting the throat and jugular veins
key_terms.يَنْحَرُونَ: Nahr — slaughter by stabbing in the upper chest/jugular notch, valid only for camels

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat cow meat slaughtered by nahr (chest-stabbing) rather than dhabh (throat-slaughter)?
ai.summary: Yunus ibn Yaqoub asked Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) about the practice of the people of Mecca, who slaughtered cattle by piercing the upper chest (nahr) rather than by the standard throat-slaughter (dhabh). The Imam responded by quoting Quran 2:71 — referring to the Bani Israel's reluctance to slaughter the cow — and then issued a clear ruling: one must only eat meat that has been properly slaughtered at the throat. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that nahr (chest-stab) is only valid for camels, not for cattle or other animals.
